kind.content: A letter on writing, reading and slow work. Every other Sunday, from Mira Okafor.

kind.alt: Marbled endpaper in navy, oxblood and gold

kind.content: Why I write by hand first
Paper is slow, and slow is the point. On first drafts that are allowed to be bad.

kind.alt: Marbled paper in forest green and copper

kind.content: The case for fewer, better notes
I kept everything for ten years and found nothing. What changed when I started throwing notes away.

kind.alt: Marbled paper in plum and ochre

kind.content: Reading slowly in a fast year
Twelve books, one pencil and a rule: nothing new until the last one has a page of notes.

kind.alt: Marbled paper in ink black and oxblood

kind.content: The white space around a page is where readers talk back. A short history of writing in books.
The margin is the only part of a book that belongs to the reader. Everything else, the author paid for.

seo.title: The Long Margin — a letter on writing, reading and slow work
